records.name: 9-1-1 Emergency Services
records.organization: Local law enforcement, fire, and EMS (Texas 9-1-1 system)
records.description_en: Call 9-1-1 for police, fire, or an ambulance when someone is in danger right now.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in Texas with an emergency or life-threatening situation.
records.how_to_apply: Dial 9-1-1 from any phone. Stay on the line and tell them where you are.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
records.notes: Source is DFPS guidance to call local law enforcement or 911 immediately for emergencies. Text-to-911 availability varies by area in Texas and was not confirmed this session; calling is the safest option.

records.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
records.description_en: Call, text, or chat with a trained crisis counselor if you are thinking about suicide, having a mental health or substance use crisis, or are worried about someone.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in emotional distress or crisis, or anyone worried about someone else.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 988, or chat online at chat.988lifeline.org.
records.notes: Text and chat are available in Spanish. TTY users can dial 711 then 988 (per Texas HHS). Deaf/hard of hearing options at 988lifeline.org.

records.name: 2-1-1 Texas
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
records.description_en: Free call that connects you to local help like food, housing, utility bills, health care, and more.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Any Texas resident who needs help finding community services.
records.how_to_apply: Dial 2-1-1 (or (877) 541-7905), chat online, or search the directory at 211texas.org.
records.notes: Toll-free alternative number: (877) 541-7905. Texas HHS also lists texting 2-1-1 as an option.

records.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
records.description_en: Talk with an advocate about abuse, safety planning, and finding local shelter and help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone experiencing domestic violence, anyone unsure about their relationship, and friends or family helping someone.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-799-7233, text START to 88788, or chat at thehotline.org.
records.notes: Spanish site: espanol.thehotline.org. Use the quick-exit button on the website if someone monitors your device.

records.name: Family Violence Service Directory
records.description_en: Online directory to find family violence programs in Texas that offer shelter, legal advocacy, counseling, and transitional housing.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Survivors of family violence in Texas and people helping them.
records.how_to_apply: Use the online directory to find the program near you, then call that program. For help right away call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at (800) 799-7233.
records.notes: TCFV is a statewide coalition, not a shelter itself. TCFV office numbers: (512) 794-1133 and toll-free (888) 450-TCFV (8238).

records.name: National Sexual Assault Hotline
records.description_en: Talk confidentially with a trained staff member about sexual assault and get connected to a local sexual assault service provider.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Survivors of sexual assault or abuse and their loved ones.
records.how_to_apply: Call 800-656-4673 or chat online at hotline.rainn.org/online.
records.notes: rainn.org blocked automated access; details confirmed on U.S. DOJ Office on Violence Against Women page.

records.name: Crisis Center Locator (Sexual Assault Programs)
records.description_en: Online tool to find sexual assault crisis centers across Texas.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Survivors of sexual assault in Texas and people helping them.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Crisis Center Locator on taasa.org to find your local rape crisis center.
records.notes: TAASA is a statewide coalition office (7700 Chevy Chase Dr., Suite 230, Austin, TX 78752), not a crisis line. For 24/7 help call RAINN (800) 656-4673.

records.name: Texas Abuse Hotline
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS)
records.description_en: Report abuse or neglect of a child, an older adult, or an adult with a disability in Texas.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone who suspects abuse, neglect, or exploitation of a child, elderly person, or adult with a disability.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-252-5400 any time, or report a non-urgent case online at TxAbuseHotline.org. Call 911 first if it is an emergency.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
records.notes: Since Sept 1, 2023, anonymous reports are not accepted; reporters must give first and last name and a phone number, but names are confidential by law. Online reports get a response within 24 hours.

records.name: Poison Help Line (Texas Poison Center Network)
records.description_en: Call for fast expert help if someone swallowed, touched, or breathed something harmful, or took the wrong medicine.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone with a possible poisoning or a question about poisons or medicines.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-222-1222 right away. Do not wait for symptoms. Call 911 if the person collapses, has a seizure, has trouble breathing, or will not wake up.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
records.notes: Answered by physicians, pharmacists, and nurses. Online tool also available at triage.webpoisoncontrol.org (National Capital Poison Center).

records.name: The Trevor Project Crisis Services
records.description_en: Talk, text, or chat with trained counselors who understand the challenges LGBTQ+ young people face.
records.eligibility_summary_en: LGBTQ+ young people in crisis or needing support.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-866-488-7386, text START to 678-678, or chat at thetrevorproject.org/get-help.

records.name: Veterans Crisis Line
records.description_en: Free, confidential crisis support for veterans, service members, and people who support them.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and their families and friends. You do not need VA benefits or health care.
records.how_to_apply: Dial 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat online.
records.notes: Family members and supporters can also call.

records.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
records.description_en: Get confidential help or report a tip if you or someone you know is being forced to work or trade sex.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Victims and survivors of human trafficking and anyone with a tip.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-888-373-7888, text 233733, or chat online.
records.notes: TTY: 711. Services offered in multiple languages. Message and data rates may apply for texts.

records.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
records.description_en: Talk with a counselor about child abuse, get support, and learn how to report abuse.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children, teens, parents, survivors, and anyone worried about a child.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 800-422-4453 (text GO), or use live chat on the website.
records.notes: To make an official report in Texas, use the Texas Abuse Hotline (800) 252-5400. Call 911 for emergencies.

records.name: Texas Youth Helpline
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS)
records.description_en: Free, confidential counseling and referrals for youth and families in crisis, including runaways.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth and teens in crisis, and their parents, guardians, and family.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-800-989-6884, or chat on the website.
records.notes: Not a reporting hotline and no law enforcement link. Offers a message service for runaways and free rides home through Operation Home Free.

records.name: National Runaway Safeline
records.description_en: Crisis support for young people who have run away, are thinking about it, or are homeless, plus help getting home safely.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth and teens in crisis, and concerned adults. Home Free free bus rides are for ages 12-21.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-800-786-2929, or chat or email through the website.

records.name: love is respect (Teen Dating Abuse Helpline)
records.organization: love is respect / The National Domestic Violence Hotline
records.description_en: Support for teens and young adults about healthy relationships and dating abuse.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Teens and young adults with questions or concerns about dating relationships.
records.how_to_apply: Call 866-331-9474, text LOVEIS to 22522, or chat on the website.

records.name: StrongHearts Native Helpline
records.description_en: Safe, anonymous support for Native Americans and Alaska Natives facing domestic or sexual violence.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Native Americans and Alaska Natives affected by domestic or sexual violence.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-844-762-8483, or chat on the website.
records.notes: Offers safety planning, advocacy, and referrals to Native-centered providers.

records.name: The Deaf Hotline
records.organization: ADWAS in partnership with The National Domestic Violence Hotline
records.description_en: Crisis help in ASL for Deaf survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Deaf survivors of abuse.
records.how_to_apply: Call by videophone at 855-812-1001.

records.name: Crisis Text Line
records.description_en: Text with a trained volunteer crisis counselor when you are struggling.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in the U.S. in emotional crisis.
records.how_to_apply: Text HOME to 741741 (HOLA for Spanish), or chat at connect.crisistextline.org/chat, or WhatsApp +1-443-787-7678.

records.name: SAMHSA National Helpline
records.organization: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
records.description_en: Free, confidential referrals to treatment, support groups, and community help for mental health and substance use problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Individuals and families facing mental health or substance use disorders.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-662-4357, or text your ZIP code to 435748.
records.notes: TTY: 1-800-487-4889. Referral service, not counseling. Uninsured callers may be referred to state-funded programs. Text service is English only.

records.name: Disaster Distress Helpline
records.organization: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
records.description_en: Crisis counseling for people upset or stressed after natural or human-caused disasters like floods, hurricanes, or shootings.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in the U.S. experiencing emotional distress related to a disaster.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-800-985-5990. For Spanish, press 2.
records.notes: Multilingual. Deaf and hard of hearing ASL callers can reach the line at the same number.

records.name: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
records.organization: HRSA (U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration)
records.description_en: Call or text for support with depression, anxiety, or stress before, during, or after pregnancy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant and new moms and their families.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-833-852-6262.
records.notes: Interpreters available in 60 languages. HRSA page blocked automated access; confirmed on Postpartum Support International site.

records.name: PSI HelpLine
records.description_en: Leave a confidential message and a trained volunteer will call or text you back with support and local resources for perinatal mood issues.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Parents and families dealing with perinatal and postpartum mental health.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-800-944-4773 (Spanish text: 971-203-7773).
records.notes: Not a crisis line; for emergencies call 911 or 988.

records.name: Trans Lifeline Hotline
records.description_en: Peer support phone line run by and for trans and nonbinary people.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Trans, nonbinary, and gender-questioning people.
records.how_to_apply: Call (877) 565-8860 during open hours.
records.notes: Will not call emergency services without your consent. Press 2 for Spanish.

records.name: VictimConnect Resource Center
records.organization: National Center for Victims of Crime
records.description_en: Confidential support, information, and referrals for victims of any crime.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Victims and survivors of crime.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 855-484-2846, or chat online.

records.name: NCMEC 24-Hour Call Center
records.organization: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
records.description_en: Report a missing child, a sighting, or child sexual exploitation.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families of missing children and anyone with information.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-843-5678. Call 911 first if a child is in immediate danger.

records.name: Local Mental Health Authority Crisis Lines
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (Local Mental Health / Behavioral Health Authorities)
records.description_en: Every Texas county has a local mental health authority with a 24/7 crisis line that can send someone to help in person.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in Texas having a mental health crisis. Services are free.
records.how_to_apply: Search your county at resources.hhs.texas.gov/pages/find-services to get your local crisis line number.
records.notes: Covers all 254 Texas counties. Offers face-to-face crisis assessment, intervention, and follow-up.

records.name: Eldercare Locator
records.description_en: Connects older adults and caregivers to local services such as meals, rides, in-home help, and elder abuse help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Older adults and their families and caregivers.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-677-1116, chat online, or email eldercarelocator@usaging.org.
records.notes: To report elder abuse in Texas, call the Texas Abuse Hotline (800) 252-5400.

records.name: TexasLawHelp.org
records.description_en: Free legal information, court forms (including protective orders), and a directory to find free legal aid in Texas.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Texans who need legal help, especially people with low income.
records.how_to_apply: Visit TexasLawHelp.org to use guides and forms, ask a question online, or find a legal aid office near you.
records.notes: Has live chat when available. Not an emergency service.
